description: Scenario tests for caption-writer. A run passes only when every item in 'expect' is satisfied. Written before the skill body (test-first).

evals.name: happy-path-instagram-saves
evals.input: Write an Instagram caption for this photo of our team shipping a feature. Goal is saves.
expect: reads brand-profile.md and voice.md before writing
writes a first line that hooks within Instagram's ~125-char preview cutoff
the body pays off the hook and is on-voice (fingerprint hit, 'never' list respected)
exactly one CTA, matched to the saves goal
uses a handful of relevant hashtags, not a wall, placed correctly
delivers 2-3 distinct options and recommends one with a rationale

evals.name: reads-foundation-and-guardrails
evals.context: voice.md bans exclamation marks and the word 'excited'; brand-profile says never hard-sell.
expect: loads voice.md and brand-profile.md
uses no exclamation marks and does not use 'excited'
does not write a hard-sell CTA
asks for platform/goal if not provided (at most 1-2 questions)

evals.name: platform-adaptation
evals.input: Give me this same post as an Instagram caption, a LinkedIn post, and an X post.
expect: does NOT paste the same caption across all three
adapts the first line, length, hashtags, and CTA to each platform's mechanics
Instagram routes any link to 'link in bio'; X uses 0-2 hashtags; LinkedIn formats for dwell
each version still sounds like the same brand voice

evals.name: goal-drives-structure
evals.input: Write two captions for this post — one to get comments, one to drive clicks.
expect: the comments version ends on a genuine, low-effort question or open loop
the clicks version teases value and uses a traffic CTA appropriate to the platform
structure and CTA visibly differ based on the goal
each has only one CTA

evals.name: complements-not-describes
evals.input: Caption for a photo of latte art at our cafe.
expect: does NOT merely describe what's in the photo
adds an angle, story, or hook the image alone doesn't convey
first line earns attention rather than narrating the visual

evals.name: thin-input-asks-minimal
expect: asks at most 1-2 essential questions (platform, goal) rather than a long form
does not invent brand specifics not in the profile
proceeds to a usable draft once it has enough

evals.name: no-link-platform-cta
evals.input: Write an Instagram feed caption to drive people to our new blog post.
expect: recognizes links aren't clickable in IG feed captions
routes the CTA to 'link in bio' rather than writing a clickable-link CTA
still makes the click feel worth it

evals.name: first-line-quality
expect: does NOT open with 'We're thrilled/excited to announce'
leads with the benefit or a hook, not fanfare
first line creates curiosity, stakes, or recognition within the cutoff
